message.content: {"passages":[{"reference":"9.1","text":"On the following day, then, Peter went out with his companions, came to the place where they had been the day before, stood there, and began to say: “God destroyed with water all the people of old who had acted impiously. Yet, finding among them all one godly man, he caused him to be saved in an ark together with his three sons and the women. From this one can perceive his nature: it takes no account of a crowd of people acting impiously, but it does not neglect the salvation of one godly person. The greatest impiety of all, then, is to abandon the sole Master of all and revere many nonexistent gods as though they existed.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"ἐν λάρνακι","chosen":"in an ark","rationale":"λάρναξ can denote a chest or coffer; the flood setting supports “ark.”"},{"source_quote":"μετὰ τριῶν αὐτοῦ υἱῶν καὶ γυναικῶν","chosen":"together with his three sons and the women","rationale":"γυναικῶν can mean “women” or “wives.” The rendering avoids specifying whose wives they were, since the Greek does not make that relationship explicit."},{"source_quote":"ὄχλου μὲν ἀσεβούντων οὐ φροντίζουσαν","chosen":"it takes no account of a crowd of people acting impiously","rationale":"The feminine participle refers back to God’s “nature”; the collective construction is represented naturally in English."},{"source_quote":"πολλοὺς τοὺς οὐκ ὄντας ὡς ὄντας σέβειν θεούς","chosen":"revere many nonexistent gods as though they existed","rationale":"This preserves both the denial that these gods exist and the contrast introduced by ὡς ὄντας."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.2","text":"“If, then, while I am instructing you and showing that this is the greatest sin, one that can destroy you all, the thought should steal into your mind that you will not be destroyed because you are many crowds, you have been deceived. For you have the example of the world that was flooded long ago. And yet their sin was much less than yours: they acted impiously against those like themselves, either by murdering or by committing adultery, but you act impiously against the God of all by revering lifeless images instead of him, or even alongside him, and by casting his divine name upon all insentient matter. In the first place, then, you have suffered misfortune by failing to recognize the difference between rule by one and rule by many: rule by one produces concord, whereas rule by many produces wars. For the one does not fight itself, but the many have occasion to launch a fight against another.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τὸν ὑμέτερον ὑποδράμῃ .νοῦν","chosen":"the thought should steal into your mind","rationale":"ὑποτρέχω here depicts a thought slipping or stealing into the mind; the printed period is treated separately as a source issue."},{"source_quote":"πολλοὶ ὄντες ὄχλοι","chosen":"because you are many crowds","rationale":"The deliberately unusual plural image is retained rather than reduced to the smoother but less exact “because you are numerous.”"},{"source_quote":"τὸ θεῖον αὐτοῦ ὄνομα πάσῃ ἀναισθήτῳ ὕλῃ ἐπιρρίψαντες","chosen":"by casting his divine name upon all insentient matter","rationale":"The rendering preserves the concrete image of ἐπιρρίπτω, “cast upon,” and takes ὕλη as physical matter rather than merely “material.”"},{"source_quote":"μοναρχίας καὶ πολυαρχίας","chosen":"rule by one and rule by many","rationale":"These expressions convey the contrast without importing the narrower modern political associations of “monarchy” and “polyarchy.”"},{"source_quote":"πρόφασιν ἔχει","chosen":"have occasion","rationale":"πρόφασις may mean a pretext, ground, or occasion; “occasion” fits the claim that plurality creates an opening for conflict."}],"source_issues":[{"source_quote":"τὸν ὑμέτερον ὑποδράμῃ .νοῦν","issue":"The selected edition prints a period between ὑποδράμῃ and νοῦν, separating the adjective and article from the noun within the phrase “your mind.” It appears to be extraneous punctuation rather than a lacuna marker; the construction remains intelligible when the period is disregarded.","proposed_reading":"τὸν ὑμέτερον ὑποδράμῃ νοῦν","blocks_publication":false}]},{"reference":"9.3","text":"“Indeed, immediately after the flood, Noah lived on for three hundred fifty years and continued in concord with the multitudes descended from him, being a king in the likeness of the only God. But after his death, many of his descendants desired kingship, and in their eagerness to reign, each devised how he might be able to do so. One sought it by war, another by deceit, another by persuasion, and another in some other way. One of them was a certain man from the lineage of Ham, who fathered Mestrem, from whom indeed the tribes of the Egyptians, Babylonians, and Persians multiplied.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"τριακόσια καὶ πεντήκοντα ἐπιζήσας ἔτη","chosen":"lived on for three hundred fifty years","rationale":"ἐπιζάω denotes continuing to live or surviving beyond an event, here the flood."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ μόνου θεοῦ κατ’ εἰκόνα ὑπάρξας βασιλεύς","chosen":"being a king in the likeness of the only God","rationale":"κατ’ εἰκόνα expresses correspondence or likeness; the wording preserves the author’s comparison between Noah’s kingship and God."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ ποιήσαντος τὸν Μεστρέμ","chosen":"who fathered Mestrem","rationale":"Although ποιέω ordinarily means “make,” the genealogical context supports the extended sense “beget” or “father.” The edition’s form Μεστρέμ is transliterated rather than harmonized with a familiar biblical name."},{"source_quote":"ἐξ οὗπερ τὰ Αἰγυπτίων καὶ Βαβυλωνίων καὶ Περσῶν ἐπλήθυνε φῦλα","chosen":"from whom indeed the tribes of the Egyptians, Babylonians, and Persians multiplied","rationale":"The nearest antecedent of οὗπερ is Mestrem, which is therefore followed in the main text; reference to Ham remains grammatically possible. The singular verb with the neuter plural φῦλα is an ordinary Greek agreement pattern."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.4","text":"“From this lineage there arose in succession a certain man named Nimrod, who had inherited magical arts. Like a giant, he chose to set his mind against God. After the flood, this man desired kingship and, being a great magician, used magical arts to compel the star of the evil one now reigning—the star that astrologically observes the world—to bestow kingship upon him. But the star, since it was a ruler and had authority over the one using force, angrily poured down the fire of kingship, so that it might both comply with the adjuration and punish the one who had first compelled it.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"μαγικὰ παρειληφὼς","chosen":"who had inherited magical arts","rationale":"παραλαμβάνω can describe receiving something through transmission or succession; μαγικά is a substantive expression for magical practices or lore."},{"source_quote":"ὥσπερ γίγας","chosen":"Like a giant","rationale":"The phrase most naturally characterizes Nimrod, though it could also color the manner in which he opposed God."},{"source_quote":"ἐναντία τῷ θεῷ φρονεῖν ἑλόμενος","chosen":"he chose to set his mind against God","rationale":"φρονεῖν concerns thought or disposition, while ἐναντία marks opposition; the rendering preserves both volition and mental hostility."},{"source_quote":"τοῦ νῦν βασιλεύοντος κακοῦ τὸν ὡροσκοποῦντα κόσμον ἀστέρα","chosen":"the star of the evil one now reigning—the star that astrologically observes the world","rationale":"ὡροσκοπέω belongs to astrological observation and literally evokes watching an hour or ascendant. Alternatives include “watches the world’s hour” and “governs the world’s horoscope”; the chosen wording is intelligible without resolving the astrological mechanism more precisely than the Greek permits."},{"source_quote":"πρὸς τὴν ἐξ αὐτοῦ βασιλείας δόσιν","chosen":"to bestow kingship upon him","rationale":"The phrase expresses the intended result, a grant of kingship proceeding from the star; the recipient is contextually Nimrod."},{"source_quote":"ὁ δὲ","chosen":"But the star","rationale":"Both ἀστήρ, “star,” and the substantival κακός, “evil one,” are masculine possible antecedents. The star is nearest and is supported by the following section’s description of the star’s stream being directed against Nimrod."},{"source_quote":"τὸ τῆς βασιλείας προσέχεε πῦρ","chosen":"poured down the fire of kingship","rationale":"The unusual source image is retained without replacing it with the later explanation that the fire was lightning."},{"source_quote":"πρός τε τὸν ὁρκισμὸν εὐγνωμονήσῃ","chosen":"comply with the adjuration","rationale":"ὁρκισμός is an adjuration or binding invocation, and εὐγνωμονέω here indicates responding favorably or compliantly to it; “honor the oath” is another possible rendering."}],"source_issues":[]},{"reference":"9.5","text":"“By this lightning bolt, then, which fell from heaven to earth, the magician Nimrod was killed and, because of what had happened, was renamed Zoroaster, since the star’s living stream had been borne against him. But the foolish among the people of that time thought that his soul had been summoned by a thunderbolt because of his friendship with God. After burying what remained of his body, they honored the tomb with a temple among the Persians, where the descent of the fire had occurred, and worshiped him as a god. Following this example, the others there also bury as friends of God those who die by lightning, honor them with temples, and erect statues representing the dead in their own forms. From this, those who gained power in their various regions similarly became imitators. Most of them honored with temples and carved images the tombs of people dear to them even when those people had not died by lightning; they also kindled altars and commanded that the dead be worshiped as gods. Much later, because so much time had passed, later generations came to believe that they really were gods.”","lexical_decisions":[{"source_quote":"διὰ τὸ τὴν τοῦ ἀστέρος κατ’ αὐτοῦ ζῶσαν ἐνεχθῆναι ῥοήν","chosen":"since the star’s living stream had been borne against him","rationale":"The rendering preserves the source’s proposed wordplay explaining the name Zoroaster through a “living” flow or stream associated with a star."},{"source_quote":"κεραυνῷ μεταπεμφθεῖσαν τὴν ψυχὴν","chosen":"his soul had been summoned by a thunderbolt","rationale":"The passive of μεταπέμπω commonly means “be sent for” or “be summoned”; “carried away” is possible contextually but is less lexically direct."},{"source_quote":"τὸν μὲν τάφον ναῷ ἐτίμησαν ἐν Πέρσαις","chosen":"they honored the tomb with a temple among the Persians","rationale":"ἐν Πέρσαις literally locates the action among the Persian people; “in Persia” would be a smoother geographical alternative."},{"source_quote":"τῶν τεθνεώτων ἰδίων μορφῶν ἱστᾶσιν ἀγάλματα","chosen":"erect statues representing the dead in their own forms","rationale":"The phrase describes images corresponding to the individual forms or likenesses of the deceased."},{"source_quote":"καὶ τῶν κατὰ τόπους οἱ δυναστεύσαντες","chosen":"those who gained power in their various regions","rationale":"The expression τῶν κατὰ τόπους is elliptical; the rendering takes it as referring to people or communities distributed place by place."},{"source_quote":"ναοῖς καὶ ξοάνοις","chosen":"with temples and carved images","rationale":"ξόανα are carved cult images, often specifically wooden, but the material is not made explicit here."},{"source_quote":"ὡς θεοὺς προσκυνεῖσθαι προσέταξαν","chosen":"commanded that the dead be worshiped as gods","rationale":"The infinitive lacks an explicit accusative subject. The deceased people whose tombs were honored are the contextual referent; taking the tombs or images themselves as the object is less likely but grammatically conceivable."}],"source_issues":[]}]}
